morphology.capsule: Generally non-capsulated (Vi capsular antigen in serovar Typhi)

habitat.naturalHabitat: Intestinal tract of humans and many animals, including poultry and reptiles
habitat.hostAssociation: Broad host range; zoonotic reservoir in poultry, eggs, and reptiles
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Can survive in water and food contaminated with feces
habitat.reservoir: Animal and human GI tract, especially poultry

culture.media: MacConkey agar, XLD (xylose lysine deoxycholate) agar, Hektoen enteric agar
culture.colonyMorphology: Colorless, non-lactose-fermenting colonies on MacConkey; black-centered colonies on XLD from H2S production

identificationClues: H2S positive — black colonies on XLD/Hektoen agar
Grows on selective enteric media such as XLD and Hektoen agar

diseases: Osteomyelitis, particularly in patients with sickle cell disease
virulenceFactors: Type III secretion systems — mediate invasion
Vi capsular antigen in serovar Typhi — antiphagocytic
clinicalImportance.transmission: Fecal-oral route — contaminated food, especially poultry and eggs, or water
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: A leading cause of foodborne bacterial gastroenteritis worldwide; typhoid fever remains a significant public health problem in areas with poor sanitation
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: H2S production and non-lactose fermentation on selective enteric media are key screening characteristics
